citation: Michal Bonczar, Jan Koszewski, Wiktor Czarnota, Martyna Dziedzic, Patryk Ostrowski, Kamil Mozdzen, Agnieszka Murawska, Pawel Hajdyla, Andrzej Walocha, Ewa Walocha, Jerzy Walocha, Mateusz Koziej. The morphology of the lumbar vertebrae: a systematic review with meta-analysis of 1481 individuals with implications for spine surgery. Surgical and Radiologic Anatomy (2025) 47:22 (article 22, pages 1 to 12). https://doi.org/10.1007/s00276-024-03509-4. Received 3 January 2024, accepted 20 November 2024, published online 6 December 2024; open access CC BY 4.0. Source: thread "Reread every paper for clinical detail", project symphony_4, 2026-10-28. Copy read: PMC open-access Cloud Service (pmc-oa-opendata), PMC11624215.1, fetched 2026-10-28; sha256 begins 38daf1a123f8f735. Printed page = PDF page (Page N of 12).
population: 1481 'individuals' (abstract: 'patients') summed from the research-group column of 18 published studies (Table 1, p. 3, PDF 3). Asia 1076 in 14 studies (UAE 50, Pakistan 26 + 81, India 302 + 120 + 50 + 12, Japan 227, China 5, Israel 97 + 55, Singapore 10 + 12, Turkey 29), Oceania 206 in 2 New Zealand studies (196, 10), Europe 199 (Spain 73, UK 126). By method: CT 8 studies 966; radiograph 5 studies 273; MRI 1 study 50; calipers 2 studies 170; 3D digitiser 2 studies 22. Living patients, cadavers (Tan: 12 Singaporean cadavers, 60 lumbar vertebrae, p. 9) and skeletal comparison samples of two Neandertal papers (Inference from ref titles 6 and 10) are pooled as one count; one source is a deer and sheep comparison (ref 34) with 5 subjects. Study mean ages 29 to 67 y; weight and height given for three studies only (Tan 2003 61.6 kg 1.66 m; Tan 2001 62 kg 1.66 m; Panjabi 1992 67.8 kg 1.678 m). Overall sex mix and age range not given. Panjabi 1992 is listed as Asia/India/radiograph in Table 1 but called Caucasian in the discussion (p. 9). Sources with pathology or anomalies are included despite the exclusion rule: spines with L5-S1 transitions (Mahato 2011, ref 20, n = 50) and subjects with and without low back pain (one Irshad 2022 paper, ref 16).
modality: Systematic review and random-effects meta-analysis (PRISMA; CATAM and AQUA named; STATISTICA 13.1, MetaXL 5.3, CMA 4.0) of published morphometry made by CT, MRI, plain radiographs, Vernier or digital calipers on dry bone and 3D digitisers on cadaveric vertebrae, pooled together because the authors say methods did not differ (p > 0.05, not shown) (pp. 3-4, PDF 3-4). Output per measure and level: pooled mean, SE, variance, 95 percent CI, Z and p against zero (Tables 2-7, pp. 5-10). Definitions only by the schematic Fig. 2 (p. 4).
levels_covered: L1 to L5, each separately, 27 measures per level (Tables 2-6, pp. 5-9, PDF 5-9), plus anterior body height and interpedicular distance by sex (Table 7, p. 10, PDF 10). No thoracic, sacral or junctional measurement. Levels numbered L1 to L5 from the top (p. 1); how source studies identified or counted levels is not stated; transitional segments not considered (p. 10).

anomalies.variant: Transitional anomalies of the lumbar spine (LSTV, sacralisation, lumbarisation, L6) and any rib or count variant
anomalies.finding: No prevalence of any anomaly is reported. The authors state that transitional anomalies were not considered and that this lowers the clinical application of the result.
anomalies.population: the whole pool, 1481 individuals from 18 studies

anomalies.variant: L5-S1 transitional segment inside a source study
anomalies.finding: Inference: one included source, Mahato 2011 (India, radiographs, n = 50, mean age 32 +/- 7.82), is titled as a radioanatomical study of spines with L5-S1 transitions, so transitional L5 or S1 segments may have entered the pooled L5 values unseparated. No count of transitions is given.
anomalies.how_identified: Inference from the reference title; radiographs

anomalies.variant: Developmental: unfused neurocentral junction and secondary ossification centres
anomalies.finding: Ossification starts about the 8th week of gestation from three primary centres (centrum forming the body; one in each neural process forming the pedicles), beginning at the thoracolumbar junction and spreading cranially and caudally; neural processes fuse to the centrum at 3 to 6 years; five secondary centres appear at puberty (spinous tip, both transverse processes, superior and inferior body surfaces), the body's centres adding to its cranio-caudal growth; ossification completes about age 25. No anomaly is tied to this.
anomalies.population: general embryology, cited from refs 19 and 35

measures.name: End-plate depth, upper and lower (EPDU, EPDL)
measures.definition: Anteroposterior extent of the cranial or caudal end plate of the body. Fig. 2 draws the EPD labels as the mediolateral span in a frontal view, but the values (31 to 34 mm) follow the usual convention depth = anteroposterior (labels swapped, Inference).
measures.projection: mixed sources: CT, MRI, radiograph, caliper, digitiser; Fig. 2 frontal view (labels swapped)
measures.page: Tables 2-6, pp. 5-9 (PDF 5-9); text pp. 4-6; Fig. 2 p. 4
measures.level_pattern: Upper 31.04 (SE 1.07), 32.12 (1.09), 33.17 (1.07), 33.83 (1.19), 34.09 (0.91) mm: monotonic rise, steps 0.3 to 1.1 mm, each about one SE or less. Lower 32.27 (1.20), 32.91 (1.17), 33.76 (1.11), 34.07 (0.95), 33.18 (1.18): rises to L4, falls at L5; L5 is the only level whose lower end plate is shallower than its upper. Inference by the paper's CI-overlap rule: no pair of levels separates, not even L1 from L5.
measures.ct_mask_recipe: Inference: body subregion; fit the cranial or caudal end-plate surface; anteroposterior axis in the end-plate plane (body centroid toward canal centroid); extent along that axis at the midsagittal line; fix whether ring apophysis and osteophytes are counted.
measures.radiograph_recipe: Inference: lateral radiograph, end-plate line from anterior to posterior cortex; magnified; the paper says nothing about projection or magnification.
measures.covariates: No sex, age or size data; Asian-weighted pool (p. 10).
measures.error: No observer error reported; SE is of the pooled mean, not of individual vertebrae.

measures.name: End-plate width, upper and lower (EPWU, EPWL)
measures.definition: Mediolateral extent of the cranial or caudal end plate. Fig. 2 draws the EPW labels as the anteroposterior span in a lateral view (swapped against the values, Inference), and the caption expands EPWL as 'End-plate depth lower'.
measures.projection: mixed sources; Fig. 2 lateral view (labels swapped)
measures.level_pattern: Upper 41.09 (1.60), 42.98 (1.57), 44.82 (1.62), 47.50 (1.87), 48.81 (1.91) mm, monotonic. Lower 43.97 (1.74), 46.10 (2.12), 49.12 (2.05), 50.63 (1.90), 49.82 (2.01): peak at L4, slight fall at L5. Lower exceeds upper within each vertebra by 2.9, 3.1, 4.3, 3.1, 1.0 mm. Inference: width/depth ratio upper 1.32 to 1.43, lower 1.36 to 1.50, L1 to L5. By the CI rule no adjacent pair separates; only upper width L1 against L5.
measures.ct_mask_recipe: Inference: same frame as depth; extent along the mediolateral axis through the end-plate centroid, or the maximum chord perpendicular to the midsagittal plane; exclude pedicle roots.
measures.radiograph_recipe: Inference: AP radiograph, body width at the end-plate line; magnified.

measures.name: Vertebral body height, anterior and posterior (VBHA, VBHP)
measures.definition: Distance between cranial and caudal end plates at the anterior cortex (VBHA) and the posterior cortex (VBHP), drawn on the lateral view of Fig. 2.
measures.levels: L1 to L5; VBHA also by sex
measures.page: Tables 2-6 pp. 5-9; Table 7 p. 10; Fig. 2 p. 4; sex text p. 9
measures.level_pattern: Anterior 24.54 (0.96), 25.75 (1.22), 26.83 (1.16), 26.86 (1.08), 27.44 (1.16) mm, rising, flat L3-L4. Posterior 26.57 (1.06), 27.02 (1.06), 26.67 (1.02), 25.76 (1.03), 24.11 (0.70): peak L2, minimum L5. Inference: VBHA/VBHP 0.92, 0.95, 1.01, 1.04, 1.14 (taller behind at L1-L2, even at L3, wedge in front at L4-L5), scale-free on a lateral view; no single height separates adjacent levels by the CI rule.
measures.ct_mask_recipe: Inference: midsagittal plane of the body subregion; cranio-caudal distance between superior and inferior end-plate surfaces along the vertebra's own axis at the anterior cortex and at the posterior cortex; exclude osteophytes.
measures.radiograph_recipe: Inference: lateral radiograph, anterior and posterior heights of the body outline; the ratio cancels magnification.
measures.covariates: VBHA men 23.66 (0.46), 24.63 (0.89), 25.90 (0.15), 25.87 (0.08), 26.92 (0.56); women 23.17 (0.03), 24.66 (0.02), 25.53 (0.61), 25.77 (0.98), 26.67 (1.44) mm (Table 7). Women exceed men only at L2 (p. 9). Inference: all male and female CIs overlap, so no level differs by the paper's rule.
measures.error: None reported; female SEs 0.03 and 0.02 and male 0.08 at L4 are implausibly small (Inference: one or two studies per cell).

measures.name: End-plate area, upper and lower (EPAU, EPAL)
measures.definition: Area of the cranial or caudal end-plate surface; Fig. 2 marks it in the axial view with an unexplained dotted contour inside the body outline.
measures.level_pattern: Upper 932.26 (56.46), 1017.74 (61.40), 1132.32 (63.14), 1151.43 (72.55), 1182.51 (65.77) mm2, monotonic. Lower 1039.83 (55.77), 1120.01 (60.84), 935.91 (401.38; CI 149.22 to 1722.59), 1199.99 (69.64), 1131.35 (61.99): L3 lower is an outlier (Inference), peak L4, L5 lower below L5 upper. Inference: area/(width x depth) 0.68 to 0.76 apart from L3 lower (0.56), below the ellipse value 0.785.
measures.ct_mask_recipe: Inference: voxel area of the body's cranial or caudal end-plate layer projected onto the end-plate plane, or the axial section about 1 mm inside the end plate; state whether the ring apophysis is included.
measures.radiograph_recipe: Not measurable on a radiograph; Inference: estimate from AP width x lateral depth x about 0.7.
measures.error: None reported; L3 lower SE 401.38 marks heterogeneity.

measures.name: End-plate inclination, transverse plane, upper and lower
measures.definition: Not defined and not drawn; degrees; reference plane and sign unknown.
measures.ct_mask_recipe: Inference: plane fit to each end-plate surface, tilt against a vertebral reference plane; cannot be matched to these numbers without the source definition.
measures.radiograph_recipe: Inference: sagittal end-plate tilt against the posterior wall on a lateral view; whether it is this measure is unknown.

measures.name: Spinal canal width (SCW)
measures.definition: Mediolateral width of the vertebral canal, drawn in the axial view of Fig. 2 across the canal.
measures.page: Tables 2-6 pp. 5-9; abstract p. 1; text pp. 4-6; discussion p. 8; conclusions p. 10
measures.level_pattern: 22.04 (0.91), 22.15 (0.94), 22.62 (0.80), 23.19 (0.82), 26.46 (0.89) mm: flat L1 to L4, step of 3.3 mm at L5. Inference by the CI rule: L5 separates from L1-L3, but L4 (21.59 to 24.79) and L5 (24.71 to 28.20) overlap by 0.08 mm; L1-L4 do not separate. The paper calls the rise progressive (pp. 1, 8, 10).
measures.ct_mask_recipe: Inference: axial slice through the pedicle isthmi; minimum distance between the medial pedicle cortices of the filled canal.
measures.radiograph_recipe: Inference: AP radiograph, interpedicular distance between inner pedicle cortices; magnified.

measures.name: Interpedicular distance (IPD), by sex
measures.definition: Not defined; named in the results text (p. 6) and Table 7 only; contributing studies not named.
measures.projection: unstated; Inference: likely AP radiograph or axial CT
measures.levels: L1 to L5, men and women separately
measures.radiograph_recipe: Inference: AP radiograph; magnified; L5 values exceed pooled L5 canal width, suggesting other studies or magnification.
measures.covariates: Men larger by 0.86, 1.11, 1.12, 0.91, 1.38 mm (3.5 to 5.1 percent); by the CI rule only L1 and L3 differ (Inference).
measures.error: None reported; L5 SEs 3.2 to 3.4 mm; several SEs implausibly small (men L1 0.12, L3 0.14; women L3 0.08).

measures.name: Spinal canal depth (SCD)
measures.definition: Anteroposterior depth of the canal in the axial view of Fig. 2, from the posterior body wall to the inner arch at the midline.
measures.level_pattern: 16.02 (1.07), 15.08 (1.00), 14.69 (0.93), 15.06 (1.04), 15.69 (1.37) mm: shallow U, minimum L3, range 1.3 mm within the SE; no level separation.
measures.ct_mask_recipe: Inference: midsagittal line of the canal at pedicle level, posterior body cortex to anterior laminar cortex or spinolaminar junction.
measures.radiograph_recipe: Inference: lateral radiograph, posterior body line to spinolaminar line; magnified.

measures.name: Spinal canal area (SCA)
measures.definition: Area of the vertebral canal in the axial view (Fig. 2).
measures.level_pattern: 251.01 (16.47), 227.28 (18.57), 213.87 (24.17), 215.45 (35.98), 245.12 (32.12) mm2: falls to a minimum at L3 and rises to L5, contrary to the discussion's progressive rise (p. 8). Inference: SCA/(SCW x SCD) 0.71, 0.68, 0.64, 0.62, 0.59, the canal turning triangular caudally (the paper calls the lumbar foramen triangular, p. 1).
measures.ct_mask_recipe: Inference: area of the filled canal in the axial slice through the pedicle isthmi.

measures.name: Pedicle width (PW), overall, right and left
measures.definition: Mediolateral width of the pedicle, drawn in the axial view of Fig. 2 from the canal edge to the lateral pedicle cortex.
measures.page: Tables 2-6 pp. 5-9; discussion pp. 7-8; abstract p. 1; conclusions p. 11
measures.level_pattern: Overall 7.51 (0.58), 8.23 (0.20), 9.71 (0.18), 11.52 (0.24), 14.58 (1.03) mm; right 7.30, 7.64, 9.56, 11.98, 15.68; left 7.73, 8.02, 9.77, 12.59, 15.93. Monotonic rise, steps 0.7, 1.5, 1.8, 3.1 mm. Inference by the CI rule: overall width separates L2|L3, L3|L4, L4|L5, not L1|L2: the best adjacent-level separator in the paper. Side values (SE 0.42 to 1.34) separate fewer pairs.
measures.ct_mask_recipe: Inference: along the pedicle axis, minimal mediolateral outer width in axial sections (isthmus), each side separately.
measures.radiograph_recipe: Inference: AP radiograph, width of the pedicle oval; magnified; the AP shadow of a converging pedicle is not its isthmus width.
measures.covariates: None reported; no left-right difference per the authors (pp. 7, 11).
measures.error: None reported; overall and side values come from different subsets (Inference).

measures.name: Pedicle height (PH), overall, right and left
measures.definition: Cranio-caudal height of the pedicle; labelled beside PW in Fig. 2 without its own arrow.
measures.page: Tables 2-6 pp. 5-9; discussion p. 7; abstract p. 1
measures.level_pattern: Overall 15.40 (0.28), 14.90 (0.19), 14.52 (0.17), 14.20 (0.34), 14.73 (1.06) mm: falls to L4, slight rise at L5. Right 15.71, 15.31, 15.31, 15.49, 18.05; left 15.47, 15.55, 14.36, 15.13, 18.16: no fall, jump at L5. Sources disagree (rise: Arora, Seema; fall: Singh, Alam; fall then rise: Wolf; Arora, Seema and Alam are not among the 18 pooled). Inference: pedicle W/H 0.49, 0.55, 0.67, 0.81, 0.99 (overall) or about 0.46 to 0.88 by side; height alone separates no adjacent pair.
measures.ct_mask_recipe: Inference: minimal cranio-caudal height between superior and inferior pedicle cortices in sagittal sections through the pedicle.
measures.radiograph_recipe: Inference: AP view, height of the pedicle oval; lateral view, pedicle between the notches; magnified.

measures.name: Pedicle area (PA), right and left
measures.definition: Area of the pedicle section; plane not stated (labelled with PW and PH in Fig. 2).
measures.ct_mask_recipe: Inference: cross-section perpendicular to the pedicle axis at the isthmus.

measures.name: Pedicle inclination, 'sagittal plane' (PIS), right and left
measures.definition: Fig. 2 (axial view) draws the angle between the midline above the spinous tip and an oblique line drawn outward from the right superior articular process, roughly along the pedicle (Inference): medial convergence measured from the sagittal plane.
measures.page: Tables 2-6 pp. 5-9; Fig. 2 p. 4; sex p. 9
measures.level_pattern: Right 10.31 (1.21), 12.21 (1.64), 18.79 (1.04), 13.90 (2.20), 21.24 (2.44) deg, rising with an L4 dip. Left 2.62 (2.31), -0.36 (3.79), -2.95 (8.26), -3.46 (5.63), -8.54 (6.96), none different from zero (p 0.22 to 0.92). Inference: left and right CIs never overlap, against the claim of no side difference (p. 1); mixed sign conventions likely.
measures.ct_mask_recipe: Inference: pedicle axis from centroids, projected on the axial plane, angle from the midsagittal plane, positive for anterior convergence, one convention for both sides.
measures.radiograph_recipe: Not measurable on a lateral; Inference: only indirect cues on AP.
measures.covariates: Alam (CT, Pakistani, not among the 18) found greater sagittal inclination in women (p. 9); not pooled.
measures.error: None reported; left SEs 2.3 to 8.3 deg.

measures.name: Pedicle inclination, 'transverse plane' (PIT), right and left
measures.definition: Fig. 2 (lateral view) draws the angle between a horizontal line and an oblique line at the pedicle: cranio-caudal tilt of the pedicle from the transverse plane (Inference).
measures.ct_mask_recipe: Inference: pedicle axis projected on the sagittal plane, angle from the end-plate plane; sign unknown.
measures.radiograph_recipe: Inference: lateral radiograph, pedicle tilt between the notches.

measures.name: Spinous process length (SPL)
measures.definition: Fig. 2 (axial view) draws it from the spinous tip to the base of the process at the laminae; values near 60 mm suggest the source reference was more anterior (Inference).
measures.ct_mask_recipe: Inference: most posterior point of the spinous subregion to a fixed anterior reference; check the reference against the Panjabi 1992 note before matching values.
measures.radiograph_recipe: Inference: lateral radiograph if the anterior reference is visible; magnified.

measures.name: Transverse process width (TPW)
measures.definition: Not drawn or defined; Inference: tip-to-tip mediolateral span of the transverse processes.
measures.page: Tables 2-6 pp. 5-9; abstract p. 1; discussion p. 8; conclusions p. 10
measures.level_pattern: 68.08 (4.59), 75.07 (2.88), 83.59 (3.39), 79.31 (4.95), 85.91 (4.08) mm: rises to L3, dips at L4, widest at L5. Inference: no adjacent pair separates by the CI rule; only L1 against L5. The paper's 'significantly widening' (p. 10) hides the L4 dip.
measures.ct_mask_recipe: Inference: mediolateral distance between the most lateral voxels of the two transverse process subregions in the vertebral frame.
measures.radiograph_recipe: Inference: AP radiograph tip to tip; magnified; tips may be faint.

measures.name: Spinous process width (SPW)
measures.definition: Drawn in the axial view of Fig. 2 across the base of the spinous process; no value reported anywhere.

level_details.detail: Smallest end plates (upper 41.09 x 31.04 mm, 932 mm2), narrowest pedicles (7.51), tallest overall pedicle height (15.40), narrowest transverse span (68.08), deepest canal (16.02) and largest canal area (251.01 mm2), body taller behind (24.54 against 26.57).
Posterior height at its peak (27.02); canal width 22.15, barely above L1; pedicle width 8.23, not separated from L1 by the CI rule (Inference).

Body about even (26.83 against 26.67); canal depth and area at minima (14.69 mm, 213.87 mm2); longest spinous process (65.67); transverse span 83.59, wider than L4; lower end-plate area outlier (935.91, SE 401.38); upper end-plate inclination dips (1.93 deg).
Lower end plate largest (50.63 x 34.07 mm, 1199.99 mm2); anterior height above posterior (26.86 against 25.76); pedicle width 11.52; transverse span dips to 79.31; right PIS dips to 13.90 deg.

Strongest anterior wedge (27.44 against 24.11); widest pedicles (14.58; by side 15.68 and 15.93) and tallest by side (18.05, 18.16); canal width 26.46 (CI touches L4's), interpedicular 30.65 men, 29.27 women; widest transverse span (85.91); lower end plate smaller than upper in depth and area (33.18 against 34.09 mm; 1131 against 1183 mm2); lower end-plate inclination 8.20 deg. May include transitional segments (not excluded; Mahato's source studied L5-S1 transitions).
level_details.page: Table 6, p. 9 (PDF 9); Table 7 p. 10; p. 10; ref 20 p. 11

level_details.detail: Not measured. Qualitative lumbar traits: large body, short thick spinous process projecting straight back, vertical facets (sagittal at first, p. 1) with superior facets facing posteromedially and medially, curved facet surfaces unlike thoracic ones, mammillary processes on the superior articular process, a canal larger than thoracic, smaller than cervical, triangular (p. 1). States lumbar disc height lies between cervical and thoracic (Inference: probably an error). Ossification begins at the thoracolumbar junction (p. 7).
Not measured; sacrum not studied. Kambin's triangle: exiting root (hypotenuse), upper end plate of the lower vertebra (base), superior articular process of the lower segment (height).

errors.what: Intra- and inter-observer error, repeatability, instrument resolution, radiographic magnification

errors.value: named in methods, never printed; bands 0-40, 30-60, 50-90, 75-100 percent, top two both called substantial

errors.what: Pooled SE (uncertainty of the random-effects mean, not individual spread)
errors.value: typical 0.2 to 2 mm for linear measures; extremes L3 lower end-plate area 401.38 mm2 (CI 149.22 to 1722.59), left PIS up to 8.26 deg, L5 IPD 3.2 to 3.4 mm
VBHA women L1 0.03, L2 0.02, men L4 0.08; IPD men L1 0.12, L3 0.14, women L3 0.08 mm (Inference: one or two studies per cell)
authors state results by method did not differ (p > 0.05) but show no comparison; limitations name differing researchers and methods as possible bias
two independent reviewers; disagreements settled by contacting authors or a third person; no agreement statistic
CATAM and AQUA named, no scores or risk-of-bias table

pearls_pitfalls.text: Pedicle width rises from 7.51 mm at L1 to 14.58 mm at L5; matching screw to pedicle matters, as a mismatch risks cortical perforation, pedicle fracture and screw loosening (citing Seema, ref 29).
Normal end-plate size guides vertebral body replacement or augmentation (vertebroplasty, kyphoplasty) and implant and prosthesis design and choice.

Canal size guides decompression (laminectomy, canal decompression): over-decompression risks instability, under-decompression may not relieve symptoms; the canal widens caudally with the transition from cord to cauda equina. No stenosis threshold is given.

Percutaneous endoscopic transforaminal discectomy (YESS) enters the disc through Kambin's triangle; indications from single herniation to stenosis, metastatic tumours, discal cysts and revision for recurrent herniation; morphometric knowledge aids navigation and lowers intraoperative complications.
Disc degeneration drives chronic low back pain; total disc replacement avoids fusion; second-generation prostheses control motion in all directions; vertebral body morphometry helps.
The pooled values are offered as normal references for diagnosing pathology and, with CT or radiographs, for choosing a prosthesis per patient.
Sex: males larger on every pooled sex measure except L2 anterior height; Singh found every measure larger in men; Alam found greater sagittal pedicle inclination in women.

Population: Tan (60 lumbar vertebrae, 12 Singaporean cadavers) found Asians larger than Panjabi's Caucasian series on numerous measures despite smaller physique; the pool is Asian-weighted (1076 of 1481).

Pitfall: Fig. 2 swaps the width and depth labels against the values, and its caption expands EPWL as 'End-plate depth lower'; PIS and PIT are named for the reference plane, not the plane of the angle (Inference from the drawing).
Pitfall: the introduction says the body is taller in front, but the pooled table shows the reverse at L1 and L2.

Pitfall: text against table: canal width and area and end-plate depth and width are said to rise steadily to L5 (p. 8), and the transverse processes to widen significantly (p. 10); the tables show canal width flat to L4, canal area lowest at L3, lower end plates largest at L4 and transverse span dipping at L4.
Pitfall: the pedicle-height debate and the sex finding of Alam draw on studies outside the 18 pooled (Arora, Seema, Alam: refs 3, 4, 29).
Pitfall: left PIS values cannot be reconciled with right; by the authors' own CI rule the sides differ at every level, against the stated absence of side differences.

instructions.text: Treat every value as a pooled adult mean, Asian-weighted (1076 of 1481), with an SE of the mean; never use the SE as a per-vertebra sigma.
Read width as mediolateral and depth as anteroposterior whatever Fig. 2's labels say.

On AP radiographs or fluoroscopy, measure each pedicle oval's width and height; use width/height as a scale-free cue, about 0.5 at L1 to 0.9-1.0 at L5 (Inference from table means); pedicle width separates L2|L3, L3|L4, L4|L5 but not L1|L2 by the CI rule; remember the AP shadow of a converging pedicle is not its isthmus width (Inference).
On a lateral view, take VBHA/VBHP: about 0.92 at L1, 0.95 at L2, 1.01 at L3, 1.04 at L4, 1.14 at L5 (Inference from means); use as a likelihood, not a rule.

On AP, use the L5 widening of the interpedicular distance (about 3.3 mm above L4 in canal width, 3.5 to 3.9 mm in IPD) as a weak cue to the last lumbar level, knowing L4 and L5 canal-width CIs overlap by 0.08 mm; never use canal width to separate L1 to L4.
Do not separate adjacent levels by canal depth, spinous process length, pedicle height, pedicle transverse-plane tilt, end-plate dimensions or transverse span.
Use transverse-process span with care: L5 widest, L3 wider than L4, L1 narrowest; check that a long process at the top is not a rib (rib check Inference).

Decide thoracic against lumbar by form: mammillary processes, vertical sagittal facets with posteromedially facing superior facets and curved surfaces, short thick straight spinous process, a larger triangular canal.
Do not assume the pooled L5 values are free of transitional segments; count from C2 or the ribs and inspect the sacrum before applying L5 priors.
Fix one sign convention for pedicle angles on both sides; do not match the left-side values of this paper.
Discard the L3 lower end-plate area; expect mask-derived area/(width x depth) near 0.68 to 0.76 (Inference).

In children and adolescents expect neural processes unfused until 3 to 6 years and five secondary centres from puberty to about 25 years; check masks for split or missing pieces there (mask behaviour Inference).
Apply a sex offset only where the paper has data: interpedicular distance (men about 0.9 to 1.4 mm wider, significant by the CI rule only at L1 and L3), none for anterior body height.
Do not treat the pooled values as a CT-specific or radiograph-specific reference: methods are pooled and the claimed lack of method difference is not shown.

bordercall: (a) Anomaly priors: none. No prevalence of LSTV, L6, T13, rib-count variants or any anomaly; transitional anomalies explicitly not considered (p. 10, PDF 10). Inference: pooled L5 values may contain transitional segments (Mahato 2011 source, ref 20).

(b) Measures overlapping Panjabi's lumbar set (Inference): end-plate width, depth, area and inclination upper and lower, anterior and posterior body height, canal width, depth and area, pedicle width, height and two inclinations, spinous process length, transverse process width; these pooled L1-L5 means are a second, Asian-weighted reference that already contains Panjabi 1992 as one of 18 sources. Additions: pedicle area by side; scale-free ratios (pedicle W/H, VBHA/VBHP, end-plate W/D, SCA/(SCW x SCD)) (Inference).

(b) Adjacent-level discrimination by the paper's CI rule (Inference from Tables 2-6): pedicle width separates L2|L3, L3|L4, L4|L5; pedicle area L4|L5 only; canal width no adjacent pair (L5 against L1-L3 only); no end-plate dimension, body height, canal depth or area, spinous length or transverse span separates any adjacent pair. Pooled-mean CIs understate individual overlap.

(b) Bias risks for mask-extracted values: swapped width/depth labels in Fig. 2; PIS/PIT named for reference planes; SPL near 60 mm implies an anterior reference beyond the laminar base; pooled CT, MRI, magnified radiographs, dry bone and cadaver digitiser data; end-plate area depends on ring apophysis and osteophyte handling; about 1 mm voxels shift widths by up to a voxel each side (last item Inference).
(c) Measurement error: none given; the pooled SE is not observer error or individual sigma; take observer error from another paper.

(d) Covariates: sex only for anterior body height (no difference by the CI rule) and interpedicular distance (men 0.86 to 1.38 mm, 3.5 to 5.1 percent, larger; significant only at L1 and L3); age, weight and height not analysed (p. 10); population Asian-weighted, with Tan's Asian series larger than Panjabi's Caucasian one (p. 9); no population covariate can be fitted (Inference).
gaps: Not reported: I-squared, studies and subjects per cell, individual SDs, method subgroups, quality scores, observer error, any measure definition beyond a schematic, how levels were counted, sex mix of the pool, SPW values, which studies gave the sex table; per-study extracted data not published (data availability statement, p. 11).

Several included sources cover only part of the measures or levels (Kadioglu, Morita and Robertson pedicles; Zhou lower lumbar; titles refs 18, 22, 27, 38), so each cell pools a different subset (Inference).

Text against table: canal area does not rise steadily (p. 8); lower end-plate depth and width do not rise to L5 (p. 8); canal width is flat to L4 and its L5 step overlaps L4 by CI (pp. 1, 8, 10); transverse span dips at L4 despite 'significantly widening' (p. 10); the anterior-taller wedge is false at L1-L2 (p. 1); no left-right difference fails for PIS by the authors' rule.
Overall against side-specific pedicle values disagree at L5 (height 14.73 against 18.05 and 18.16) and in trend (Tables 2-6); Inference: different source subsets.

Table 1 lists Panjabi 1992 as Asia, India, radiograph, while the discussion calls it Caucasian (p. 3 against p. 9); Inference from memory: Panjabi measured 12 cadaveric spines with a 3D digitiser in the USA, so Asia would be 1064 and radiograph 261.
Table 1 years against references: Tan 2001 row = ref 32 (2002), Tan 2003 row = ref 33 (2004), Singh 2021 row = ref 30 (2022); which Irshad paper is (a) or (b) is not stated.
Exclusion of pathology against included sources: L5-S1 transitions (ref 20), low back pain (ref 16), Neandertal comparisons (refs 6, 10), deer and sheep comparison (ref 34).
L3 lower end-plate area (935.91, CI 149.22 to 1722.59) incompatible with L3 lower width and depth.
Fig. 2 caption expands EPWL as 'End-plate depth lower'; empty citation brackets on p. 2; search strings spell 'lumber spine' (p. 2), though 'lumbar vertebrae' is spelled correctly in each.

Against other papers (Inference from memory): Panjabi's lumbar pedicle convergence rises to about 30 deg at L5 against 21 deg here (right) and no rise on the left; Eisenstein's lower normal midsagittal canal near 15 mm against pooled means of 14.7 to 16.0 mm, suggesting a different measure or mixed cohorts; classical anatomy gives L3 the longest transverse processes, here L5 span is widest.
